name: RWKV: Reinventing RNNs for the Transformer Era
problem: Transformers parallelise during training but are quadratic and memory-hungry at inference; RNNs are linear and constant-memory at inference but do not parallelise during training. Architecture families are usually a choice, not both.
mechanism: RWKV is formulated so the SAME model is a Transformer during training and an RNN during inference: a linear-attention formulation with time-mixing (WKV) and channel-mixing blocks, plus a receptance-gated formulation that lets the recurrence be expressed in a numerically stable closed form with no time-step hyperparameter. Constant memory and constant compute per token at inference.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claims (abstract): scaled to 14B parameters, 'by far the largest dense RNN ever trained', performing ON PAR with similarly sized Transformers. That is a quality claim, not a speedup: the abstract states constant computational and memory complexity during inference without attaching a multiplier or a baseline engine.
